title: Thunderbird mail profiles (Snap install)
whyItMatters: The Snap version of Thunderbird keeps its profiles under the snap folder instead of ~/.thunderbird, with the local mail copy, address book, calendar and saved account passwords, and is easy to miss.
source: Ubuntu ships Thunderbird as a Snap since 24.04, and Mozilla Support places the profile at ~/snap/thunderbird/common/.thunderbird: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/1469510
notes: Matches the profile folders only, not the mailbox files inside them. Ubuntu 24.04 switched the default Thunderbird to the Snap and did not always migrate an existing ~/.thunderbird, so both locations can hold data; Flatpak builds use ~/.var/app/org.mozilla.thunderbird/.thunderbird (standard release) or ~/.var/app/org.mozilla.thunderbird_esr/.thunderbird (ESR), and the older id org.mozilla.Thunderbird is still on Flathub.

cleanup.exportFirst: Export the address book and calendars from Thunderbird, and copy the profile folder to a backup drive, before anything is removed.
cleanup.signOut: Remove the mail accounts in Thunderbird's account settings, so no saved password or login token for these mailboxes stays on the computer.
steps: Uninstall the Thunderbird snap from the App Center or with the Snap Store app.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Deletes the local copy of all mail, address books, calendars and saved account passwords in the snap profiles. Mail on the server is not affected.
cleanup.source: Mozilla Support, Profiles - Where Thunderbird stores your messages and other user data: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data
